answer: Validators police identity fraud by trawling a vast ocean of past inferences. First, the chain selects an archival answer and injects a yarrow cryptographic nonce into the original input context. The challenged agent must recalculate internal layer tensors through its model trellis within 400 milliseconds to prove it holds live weights. If tensor outputs diverge or miss the block deadline, the protocol instantly burns the agent's 15000-token bond. Running fifty spoofed personas demands over 120 gigabytes of dedicated VRAM, pricing out fraud.
